newsitem.title: NORWAY: ATHLETICS-GEBRSELASSIE REOPENS ASSAULT ON 10,000M RECORD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GEBRSELASSIE REOPENS ASSAULT ON 10,000M RECORD.

text.p: Haile Gebrselassie reopens an assault on Friday on a world record which has been transformed in the past four years.

The little Ethiopian will attempt to regain the 10,000 metres world record from Morocco's Salah Hissou in the highlight race of the Bislett Games, opening event in the Golden Four grand prix meetings.
Sixty world records have tumbled at the Bislett Games and a 61st to Gebrselassie on Friday would complete a hat-trick at the stadium over the longest track distance.
In 1993, Kenya's Yobes Ondieki made history at the Bislett Games by breaking the 27-minute barrier over 10,000 metres for the first time.
Ondieki reduced the previous mark of 27 minutes 07.91 seconds set by compatriot Richard Chelimo to 26:58.38.
In the following year, again at the Bislett Games, another Kenyan, William Sigei, transferred his cross country prowess to the track by slashing the record to 26:52.53.
Gebrselassie made a mockery of that time in 1995 with 26:43.53 in the Dutch town of Hengelo, only for Hissou to clock an equally astounding 26:38.08 in Brussels last year.
Now Gebrselassie, Olympic champion and twice world gold medallist over 10,000, wants the mark back.
After winning the world indoor 3,000 title in Paris last March by more than four seconds, Gebrselassie was given the chance to become the first man to win $1,000,000 in a track race.
Gebrselassie took on Olympic and world 1,500 gold medallist Noureddine Morceli in Hengelo over two miles with a million dollars promised to the man who finished first in a time under eight minutes.

Morceli, clearly not race fit, dropped out early, the pace-making was not to Gebrselassie's satisfaction and the Ethiopian eventually finished outside the target in 8:01.08, enough though to retrieve his world record from Kenya's Daniel Komen.
"Now I've got my two miles record back I want the 10,000," he said.

Olympic and world 100 metres champion Donovan Bailey, comprehensively beaten by American champion Maurice Greene, in Lausanne on Wednesday, steps up to 200 at a meeting traditionally dedicated to the middle and long distances.

Hicham el Guerrouj, who fell in the Olympic 1,500 final last year, is the man in form for the Dream Mile while the new American champion Marion Jones takes on Olympic gold medallist Gail Devers in the women's 100.
Devers, who is not in the U.S. team for next month's world championships in Athens, defeated Jones while setting a year's best of 10.89 seconds in Lausanne on Wednesday.
The most attractive field event of the evening will be the men's javelin which features world and Olympic champion Jan Zelezny against the silver medallist Steve Backley.
